chunks.title: PHẦN 1: THUẬT TOÁN PHÂN LUỒNG ESI (ESI TRIAGE ALGORITHM LOGIC)
chunks.issuing_body: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
chunks.page_content:
*(Trích xuất và chuẩn hóa từ Figure 2-1, 2-2 và các Text blocks)*

*   **Decision Point A:** Requires immediate lifesaving intervention?
    *   **Yes** ➔ **ESI 1**
    *   **No** ➔ Move to B
*   **Decision Point B:** High-risk situation? OR Confused/lethargic/disoriented? OR Severe pain/distress?
    *   **Yes** ➔ **ESI 2**
    *   **No** ➔ Move to C
*   **Decision Point C:** How many different resources are needed?
    *   **None** ➔ **ESI 5**
    *   **One** ➔ **ESI 4**
    *   **Many** ➔ Move to D
*   **Decision Point D:** High-risk vital signs? (Reassess acuity)
    *   **Yes** ➔ Upgrade/Consider **ESI 2**
    *   **No** ➔ **ESI 3**

---

chunks.title: PHẦN 2: GIẢI THÍCH CHI TIẾT CÁC ĐIỂM QUYẾT ĐỊNH (DECISION POINTS)
chunks.issuing_body: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
chunks.page_content:
**A. Immediate lifesaving intervention required:** 
Airway or respiratory support, emergency medications, hemodynamic interventions such as fluid resuscitation or blood products. Clinical presentations requiring lifesaving interventions include the following: intubated, unresponsive, pulselessness, apneic, severe respiratory distress, profound hypotension or hypoglycemia. 
*Unresponsiveness is defined as a patient who either:*
1. Is nonverbal and not following commands (acutely) OR 
2. Requires noxious stimulus (P or U on AVPU scale).

**B. High-risk situation:** 
May become unstable, have high risk for deterioration, or exhibit newly altered mental status. Severe pain or distress is determined by patient report, corroborated with clinical observation.

**C. Resources:** 
Count the number of *different types* of resources, not the individual tests or radiographs. *(For example: complete blood count, electrolytes, and coagulant studies = 1 resource because they are all lab tests. CBC + chest radiograph = 2 resources).*

**D. High-risk vital signs:** 
Reassess to determine whether the patient warrants a higher acuity level if a patient has one or more vital signs outside the normal parameters for the patient.

---

chunks.title: Bảng 1: Examples of Lifesaving Interventions (Table 3-1)
chunks.issuing_body: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
chunks.page_content:
| Intervention Type | Lifesaving Interventions |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Airway/breathing** | Assisted ventilation, Intubation, Surgical airway, Emergent non-invasive positive pressure ventilation |
| **Electrical Therapy** | Defibrillation, Emergent cardioversion, External pacing |
| **Procedures** | Chest needle decompression, Pericardiocentesis, Open thoracotomy |
| **Hemodynamics** | Significant intravenous fluid resuscitation, Blood administration, Control of external hemorrhage |
| **Medications** | Adenosine, Atropine, Dextrose, Dopamine, Epinephrine (including IM for anaphylaxis), Naloxone |

chunks.title: Bảng 2: Predicted ESI Resources (Table 5-1 & Figure 2-2)
chunks.issuing_body: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
chunks.page_content:
| ESI Resources (Counted) | NOT ESI Resources (Not Counted) | | :--- | :--- | | • Labs (blood, urine)
• Electrocardiogram, radiographs
• CT, MRI, ultrasound, angiography
• Intravenous fluids (hydration)
• IV, IM, or nebulized medications
• Specialty consultation
• Simple procedure = 1 (laceration repair, urinary catheter)
• Complex procedure = 2 (procedural sedation) | • History and physical exam (including pelvic)
• Point-of-care testing
• Saline or heparin lock
• Oral medications
• Tetanus immunization
• Prescription refills
• Phone call to primary care physician
• Simple wound care (dressings, recheck)
• Crutches, splints, slings |

chunks.title: Bảng 3: Patient Presentations and Predicting Resources (Table 5-2)
chunks.issuing_body: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
chunks.page_content:
| ESI Level | Patient Presentation | Interventions | Resources |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **5** | Healthy 3-year-old with right ear pain, up to date on immunizations. Vitals WNL. | Needs an exam and prescription | None |
| **5** | 42-year-old who lost rescue inhaler, needs new prescription. Asymptomatic, vitals WNL. | Needs an exam and prescription | None |
| **4** | Healthy 19-year-old with a sore throat. Vitals WNL. | Needs an exam, culture(s), prescriptions | One |
| **4** | Healthy 29-year-old assigned female at birth with dysuria. Vitals WNL. | Needs an exam, urine, urine culture, maybe urine pregnancy, and prescriptions | One |
| **3** | 22-year-old assigned male at birth with RLQ abdominal pain since morning. Vitals WNL. | Needs exam, labs, IV fluid, abdominal CT scan, perhaps surgical consult | Two or more |
| **3** | 45-year-old with left lower leg pain and swelling after 12-hr car trip. Vitals WNL. | Needs exam, labs, lower extremity non-invasive vascular studies | Two or more |
*(Lưu ý: WNL = Within Normal Limits)*

| Preschooler, 3–5 years | 65–120 | 18–35 | 89–112 |

| Adolescent, 12–18 years | 60–100 | 12–20 | 100–130 |
